| `type`      | Shape                                                                             | Notes                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`      | `{ "type": "text", "text": "..." }`                                               | Plain text.                                                                                                                                    |
| `image_url` | `{ "type": "image_url", "image_url": "..." | { "url": "...", "detail": "..." } }` | Multimodal. Requires `--mmproj` and the `mtmd` Cargo feature. The URL must be a local file path or a `file://` URL.                            |
| `audio_url` | `{ "type": "audio_url", "audio_url": "..." }`                                     | Multimodal. **Currently rejected** by the multimodal bitmap loader (`unsupported multimodal chat content part type`). Reserved for future use. |
| `video_url` | `{ "type": "video_url", "video_url": "..." }`                                     | Same as `audio_url` — reserved, currently rejected.                                                                                            |

### Templates

The `template` field selects a built-in chat template (`main.rs:2381`). Names are matched case-insensitively. Unknown names fall back to `chatml`. The recognized built-ins drive the prompt renderer and the tool-call format:

| Template           | Tool format             |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `chatml` (default) | `ToolFormat::ChatMl`    |
| `mistral-instruct` | `ToolFormat::Mistral`   |
| `plain`            | `ToolFormat::Plain`     |
| everything else    | `ToolFormat::default()` |

### Tools

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "city": { "type": "string" } },
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`type` must be `"function"`. `function.parameters` is a JSON Schema; when omitted the server substitutes an empty object schema `{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[]}`.

`tool_choice` accepts `"none"`, `"auto"`, or an object of the form `{"name": "tool"}` / `{"function": {"name": "tool"}}`. If the named tool is not present in `tools` the server returns `400 tool_choice references unknown tool: <name>`. `function_call` is validated with the same logic.

### Response body (`ChatResponse`, `main.rs:376`)

```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-1749900000",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1749900000,
  "model": "llama-crab",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "llama-crab is a Rust binding to llama.cpp.",
        "tool_calls": []
      },
      "logprobs": null,
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 18, "completion_tokens": 9, "total_tokens": 27 }
}
```

When tool calls are extracted from the model's output, `content` is `null` and `tool_calls` is populated:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": null,
    "tool_calls": [
      {
        "id": "call_0",
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "get_weather",
          "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "finish_reason": "tool_calls"
}
```

`finish_reason` is `stop`, `length`, or `tool_calls`. Chat logprobs (when `logprobs: true`) are returned as `{ content: [...], refusal: null }` with per-token `token`, `logprob`, `bytes` (`bytes` is always `null`) and `top_logprobs`.

### Example

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "local-chat",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "system", "content": "Answer briefly." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "What is llama-crab?" }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0.7
  }'
```

## `POST /v1/embeddings`

Requires the server to be started with `--embeddings` or `--reranking` (`main.rs:1817`).

### Request body (`EmbeddingRequest`, `main.rs:450`)

| Field             | Type                    | Required | Default   | Notes                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `model`           | string                  | No       | ignored   | —                                                                                    |
| `input`           | string \| string []     | **Yes**  | —         | One text or a batch.                                                                 |
| `user`            | string                  | No       | ignored   | —                                                                                    |
| `normalize`       | boolean                 | No       | `false`   | L2-normalizes the embedding.                                                         |
| `encoding_format` | `"float"` \| `"base64"` | No       | `"float"` | `base64` returns little-endian f32 bytes encoded as a single base64 string per item. |

### Response body (`EmbeddingResponse`, `main.rs:463`)

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "object": "embedding", "embedding": [0.0123, -0.0456, ...], "index": 0 },
    { "object": "embedding", "embedding": [0.0789, 0.0234, ...], "index": 1 }
  ],
  "model": "local-embed",
  "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 4 }
}
```

The `usage` object intentionally does not include `completion_tokens` (it's a text-input endpoint). When `encoding_format: "base64"` is used, each item gains an `"encoding_format": "base64"` field and the `embedding` is a base64-encoded string of 4-byte little-endian f32 values.

### Example

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "local-embed",
    "input": ["first document", "second document"],
    "normalize": true,
    "encoding_format": "float"
  }'
```

## `POST /v1/rerank` (and aliases)

Requires `--reranking`. Four paths share the same handler: `/v1/rerank`, `/v1/reranking`, `/rerank`, `/reranking`.

### Request body (`RerankRequest`, `main.rs:500`)

| Field       | Type      | Required | Default | Notes                                           |
| ----------- | --------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `model`     | string    | No       | ignored | —                                               |
| `query`     | string    | **Yes**  | —       | —                                               |
| `documents` | string [] | **Yes**  | —       | Non-empty.                                      |
| `top_n`     | integer   | No       | all     | Truncate the result list to the top N by score. |

### Response body (`RerankResponse`, `main.rs:512`)

```json
{
  "model": "local-reranker",
  "results": [
    { "index": 0, "document": "Runs on your machine", "relevance_score": 0.8712 },
    { "index": 1, "document": "Hosted API", "relevance_score": 0.0234 }
  ]
}
```

Results are sorted by `relevance_score` descending. `document` is included for every result; the wire shape uses `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` on the field but in practice it is always populated.

### Example

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/rerank \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "local-reranker",
    "query": "local inference",
    "documents": ["Runs on your machine", "Hosted API"],
    "top_n": 1
  }'
```

## Extras

### `POST /extras/tokenize`

Tokenize text using the loaded model's vocabulary.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/extras/tokenize \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "input": "hello" }'
```

```json
{ "tokens": [15339, 29888] }
```

### `POST /extras/tokenize/count`

Return only the token count.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/extras/tokenize/count \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "input": "hello" }'
```

```json
{ "count": 2 }
```

### `POST /extras/detokenize`

Convert a token id list back to text. Token ids are `i32` to match the llama.cpp vocabulary representation; negative ids and reserved tokens are accepted.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/extras/detokenize \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "tokens": [15339, 29888] }'
```

```json
{ "text": "hello" }
```

## Sampling fields

These are flattened into the top level of both `CompletionRequest` and `ChatRequest` (`SamplingRequest`, `main.rs:246`). All are optional and override the corresponding defaults of `SamplingOptions::default()` (completions) or `SamplingOptions::chat()` (chat completions).

| Field               | Type    | Notes                                 |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `temperature`       | `f32`   | Sampler temperature.                  |
| `top_k`             | `i32`   | Top-K truncation.                     |
| `top_p`             | `f32`   | Nucleus sampling.                     |
| `tfs_z`             | `f32`   | Tail-free sampling.                   |
| `min_p`             | `f32`   | Minimum-p sampling.                   |
| `typical_p`         | `f32`   | Typical-p sampling.                   |
| `min_keep`          | `usize` | Minimum number of candidates to keep. |
| `penalty_last_n`    | `i32`   | Window for repeat penalty.            |
| `repeat_penalty`    | `f32`   | Repeat penalty multiplier.            |
| `frequency_penalty` | `f32`   | OpenAI-style frequency penalty.       |
| `presence_penalty`  | `f32`   | OpenAI-style presence penalty.        |
| `mirostat_mode`     | `i32`   | `0` disables mirostat.                |
| `mirostat_tau`      | `f32`   | Mirostat target entropy.              |
| `mirostat_eta`      | `f32`   | Mirostat learning rate.               |
| `seed`              | `u32`   | Deterministic seed.                   |

## Structured output

`StructuredRequest` (`main.rs:280`) is resolved by `grammar_text` (`main.rs:2339`) in this priority order:

1. `grammar` — raw GBNF grammar. Used verbatim when non-empty.
2. `json_schema` — JSON Schema converted to GBNF via `json_schema_grammar`.
3. `response_format`— accepts:
   - `{ "type": "text" }` — no grammar.
   - `{ "type": "json_object" }` — the global `json_object_grammar()` unless `schema` is present, in which case the schema is converted.
   - `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "schema": ... } }` — schema-backed grammar. `schema` may also be provided at the top level of `response_format`.
   - Any other type — `400` error: `unsupported response_format type: <v>`.
4. `grammar_root` — the GBNF root rule name (default `"root"`).

The grammar sampler is then chained with the base sampler (`build_request_sampler`, `main.rs:2321`).

## Error envelope

Non-streaming routes return errors as JSON:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "n must be greater than zero",
    "type": "invalid_request"
  }
}
```

| Status             | Trigger                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`              | Worker validation failure (see below).                                      |
| `500`              | Job channel closed or oneshot reply dropped.                                |
| `400` (plain text) | Axum JSON deserialization failure (malformed body, missing required field). |

Validation failures that surface as `400 invalid_request` include:

- `n must be greater than zero`
- `best_of must be greater than zero`
- `best_of must be greater than or equal to n`
- `encoding_format must be 'float' or 'base64', got '<v>'`
- `unsupported logit_bias_type: <v>`
- `invalid logit_bias token id: <k>`
- `unsupported response_format type: <v>`
- `response_format json_schema requires a schema`
- `tool_choice references unknown tool: <name>`
- `function_call references unknown tool: <name>`
- `unsupported chat tool type: <v>`
- `unsupported chat content part type: <v>`
- `unsupported stop sequence value: <v>`
- `reranking endpoint not enabled (start with --reranking)`
- `multimodal chat content requires --mmproj`
- `multimodal chat content requires llama-crab-server built with the 'mtmd' feature`
- `logprobs are not supported for multimodal chat`

## Versioning

The OpenAI-compatible routes and the schemas above first shipped in &#x2A;*0.1.4 (2026-06-14)**; the 0.1.5 release only moved the documentation site and did not touch the server; &#x2A;*0.1.6 (2026-06-15)** added opt-in Hugging Face support to the server — the `hf-hub` Cargo feature and the `--hf-filename` / `LLAMA_CRAB_HF_FILENAME` flag — without changing the OpenAI route surface. The full changelog is at [`llama-crab/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/DominguesM/llama-crab/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Streaming

Both text and chat completions support streaming. Set `"stream": true` on the request body to receive server-sent events (SSE) instead of a single JSON response. The streaming path is implemented in `crates/llama-crab-server/src/main.rs` at the `completions` and `chat_completions` handlers, and the SSE adapter is `sse_response` (`main.rs:2481`).

## SSE envelope

Every frame is one of:

| Frame shape                             | When emitted                              |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `data: {…JSON…}\n\n` (default `event:`) | A `StreamFrame` from the worker.          |
| `event: error\ndata: <message>\n\n`     | The worker reported a failure mid-stream. |
| `data: [DONE]\n\n`                      | Always the last frame.                    |

The `[DONE]` sentinel is **always** emitted at the end of the stream, even after an `error` event (`main.rs:2504`). Clients should consume frames by reading the `data:` field and stop when the value equals `[DONE]`. Treat any `event: error` frame as a failed request.

The HTTP response uses the standard `text/event-stream` content type, set by `axum::response::sse::Sse`. The server installs `KeepAlive::default()` (`main.rs:2491`) — axum sends a comment-only frame every \~15 seconds to keep the connection open through intermediaries.

## `object` discriminators

The streaming frames mirror the OpenAI wire format. The `object` field on each frame tells the client which decoder to use:

| Endpoint                                     | `object` value          | Body field with content    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `POST /v1/completions` (`stream: true`)      | `text_completion`       | `choices[0].text`          |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` (`stream: true`) | `chat.completion.chunk` | `choices[0].delta.content` |

## Chat streaming

```bash
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "local-chat",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Count to three." }],
    "max_tokens": 32
  }'
```

The stream starts with a role-announce frame:

```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-1749900000",
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
  "created": 1749900000,
  "model": "llama-crab",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "delta": { "role": "assistant" },
      "finish_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Subsequent frames carry content deltas in `choices[0].delta.content`:

```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-1749900000",
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
  "created": 1749900000,
  "model": "llama-crab",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "delta": { "content": "One" },
      "finish_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

When the model emits a tool call, the server parses the running text through a `ToolCallStream` (`main.rs:1620`). The text is split into `delta.content` frames (text-only path) and `delta.tool_calls` frames (tool path). Content frames are suppressed while a tool call is being assembled — once a tool call starts, all subsequent text becomes part of the tool arguments and is delivered as `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments`. When the call finishes, content frames resume only if the model returns to plain text.

A tool-call delta frame looks like:

```json
{
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "delta": {
        "tool_calls": [
          {
            "index": 0,
            "id": "call_0",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
              "name": "get_weather",
              "arguments": "{\"city\":\""
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      "finish_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Subsequent deltas for the same tool call reuse the same `index` and may omit `id` and `type`. The `stream_frame_tool_call_delta` helper (`main.rs:2436`) drops a frame entirely when none of `id`, `name`, or `arguments` is set.

The final chat frame has an empty `delta` and a `finish_reason` of `stop`, `length`, or `tool_calls`. The same identifier (`id`), `created` timestamp, and `model` are reused across every frame of a single stream.

### Chat logprobs in streams

When the request sets `logprobs: true` (with optional `top_logprobs`), per-token logprobs are attached to each stream frame in `choices[0].logprobs`:

```json
"logprobs": {
  "content": [
    { "token": "One", "logprob": -0.4, "bytes": null,
      "top_logprobs": [{ "token": "One", "logprob": -0.4, "bytes": null }, ...] }
  ],
  "refusal": null
}
```

The wire shape matches the OpenAI chat logprobs format. `bytes` and `refusal` are always `null` (the server does not yet emit token-byte breakdowns or refusal content).

## Text completion streaming

```bash
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "local",
    "stream": true,
    "prompt": "One short sentence:",
    "max_tokens": 32
  }'
```

Each frame uses `object: "text_completion"` and carries the generated text in `choices[0].text`:

```json
{
  "id": "cmpl-1749900000",
  "object": "text_completion",
  "created": 1749900000,
  "model": "llama-crab",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "text": "The quick brown fox",
      "logprobs": null,
      "finish_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

The final frame carries an empty `text` and a `finish_reason` of `stop`, `length`, or `tool_calls`. When `logprobs` was set on the request, each frame's `choices[0].logprobs` mirrors the non-streaming `CompletionLogprobsResponse` shape (`tokens`, `text_offset`, `token_logprobs`, `top_logprobs`).

::callout{color="warning" icon="i-lucide-alert-triangle"}
Streaming text completions accept 

**exactly one prompt**

. A 

`prompt`

 array with more than one entry causes a mid-stream 

`error`

 frame followed by 

`[DONE]`

 (

`main.rs:1017-1024`

).
::

## Error frames

When the worker fails after the SSE response has started, the stream emits:

```text
event: error
data: <plain error message>
```

followed by the usual `data: [DONE]` terminator. The data is the worker's error string verbatim — there is no JSON envelope, and no `error` type. Common triggers include:

- Prompt evaluation failures (e.g. context overflow).
- Multimodal bitmap load errors.
- Stream control requests that abort generation.

## Client guidance

A minimal browser or Node SSE reader should:

1. Read each `data:` frame.
2. Stop when the data is `[DONE]`.
3. Treat any `event: error` frame as a failed request.
4. For chat, append `choices[0].delta.content` (and append tool-call deltas when present).
5. For text completions, append `choices[0].text` when present.
6. Use the `object` field to switch between text and chat decoders.

The server does not provide a per-frame usage summary. Compute token usage from the non-streaming response (the same request with `stream: false`) if you need it, or rely on the framework's tokenizer separately.

## Behaviour changes vs. 0.1.4

Streaming is part of the server's 0.1.4 introduction; no breaking changes to the SSE protocol have shipped in 0.1.5. The 0.1.4 release added the high-level streaming completion APIs (`create_completion_stream`, `CompletionChunk`, `StreamControl`) used by the worker on the server side. The wire protocol is the same in 0.1.5.


# Operations

`llama-crab-server` is a single-model HTTP process. There is no multi-model routing, no request rate limiting, and no built-in metrics endpoint — operationally, treat each process as one loaded GGUF running on one synchronous worker thread.

## Process model

The binary is a tokio + axum application whose entire inference path lives on a single dedicated thread named `llama-crab-worker`. The structure is:

1. `main` initialises `tracing_subscriber`, parses the CLI, and binds the TCP listener (`main.rs:645-686`).
2. `spawn_worker` (`main.rs:826`) calls `Llama::load` on the worker thread. If loading fails, the worker exits and `main` returns an error **before** binding the port — the server never serves requests in a degraded state.
3. With the worker running, the HTTP `Router` is built and `axum::serve` starts accepting connections.
4. Each HTTP handler sends a `Job` over a `std::sync::mpsc` channel and awaits a `oneshot::Receiver` (or, for streaming, a `tokio_mpsc::UnboundedReceiver` of `StreamFrame`).
5. The worker processes one `Job` at a time in a `for job in rx` loop. There is no queueing, no concurrency, and no preemption — a long completion blocks all subsequent requests.

Because the worker is synchronous and the HTTP layer is async, the server must be `cargo run` with the default `rt-multi-thread` tokio runtime. The axum `serve` call does not install a graceful-shutdown handler, so `Ctrl+C` aborts the process via tokio's default behaviour.

## Startup banner

On a successful start the binary writes a banner to stderr (`main.rs:676-683`):

```text
llama-crab-server listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
  model : llama-crab
  routes: /health, /v1/models, /v1/completions, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank, /extras/tokenize, /extras/tokenize/count, /extras/detokenize
  ctrl+c to stop
```

The route list is hard-coded in the banner and does not include the alias paths `/v1/reranking`, `/rerank`, and `/reranking` even though they are registered. Parse the live process to enumerate every available path (see [Health and readiness](https://dominguesm.github.io/#health-and-readiness)).

## Health and readiness

### Liveness

`GET /health` (`main.rs:690`) is a static response that does not inspect the worker:

```bash
curl -f http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

```json
{ "status": "ok" }
```

The handler returns `200 OK` as long as the axum process is running. A failure here means the process is down or unreachable, not that the model failed to load.

### Model verification

`GET /v1/models` returns the loaded model. Use it to confirm that the right `--model-name` is being advertised and to verify the process is past model loading:

```bash
curl -f http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models
```

### Deep readiness

For deployment readiness, run a small request that matches the model's role. A text completion with a short prompt, an embedding call, or a rerank call all exercise the worker end-to-end. `/health` alone is not enough — a worker that crashed after `spawn_worker` returned would still respond to `/health` with `200 OK` while failing every real request.

A pragmatic readiness check:

```bash
# Adjust the role to match the deployment.
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"llama-crab","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"max_tokens":4}'
```

## Logging

The server uses `tracing_subscriber::fmt` with an `EnvFilter` (`main.rs:646-651`). Without `RUST_LOG`, the filter is `info`. Useful levels:

```bash
# Default — startup banner and the listen event.
RUST_LOG=info llama-crab-server --model /models/model.gguf

# Verbose — request-level tracing from tower_http::trace::TraceLayer.
RUST_LOG=llama_crab_server=debug,tower_http=info llama-crab-server --model /models/model.gguf
```

`TraceLayer::new_for_http()` is enabled by default (`main.rs:673`). With the default config it emits request/response lifecycle events at `DEBUG`/`INFO`/`TRACE` — set `RUST_LOG=tower_http=info` (or `debug`) to surface them. The layer does not include request bodies.

## Capacity planning

### One model per process

`llama-crab-server` is a single-model server. To serve multiple models, run multiple processes on different ports and route at a higher layer (e.g. nginx, a sidecar proxy, or a custom gateway). Each process owns its own `Llama` instance and KV cache, with no shared state between them.

### Tuning knobs

| Flag                          | Effect                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--n-ctx`                     | Context window. Larger contexts cost memory and may force longer prefill latencies.                                                                         |
| `--n-batch`                   | Prompt-processing batch size. Larger values use more memory but reduce prefill time.                                                                        |
| `--n-threads`                 | CPU decode threads. Set to the number of physical cores; with mobile presets also drives batch threads.                                                     |
| `--n-gpu-layers`              | Number of transformer layers to offload. Tune until the model fits in VRAM and decode latency stops improving.                                              |
| `--mobile-preset`             | Coordinated trade-off (`low-ram`, `balanced`, `gpu-max`) that replaces the legacy `n_*` defaults with mobile-tuned values.                                  |
| `--pooling`                   | Embedding / reranking pooling strategy. Required for some models (`mean` for BGE, `rank` for cross-encoders).                                               |
| `--embeddings`, `--reranking` | Load the model in embedding or reranking mode. Must be set at startup; the worker rejects embedding/rerank requests when the corresponding flag is not set. |

### Memory and concurrency

The worker is single-threaded; the server does not pipeline requests. A long generation blocks every other request (their jobs queue in the mpsc channel but their `rx.await` resolves only after the in-flight job returns). For mixed workloads, run multiple processes and load-balance at the HTTP layer.

The server applies no `RequestBodyLimitLayer` or request timeout. Multi-GB JSON bodies and unbounded request durations are accepted. Place a reverse proxy in front of the process if you need to enforce either.

## Observability gaps

`llama-crab-server` does not expose Prometheus metrics, a `/metrics` endpoint, an OpenTelemetry exporter, or structured request logs. The only observability surface is `tracing`:

- The startup banner on stderr.
- A single `tracing::info!` line on `listen` (`main.rs:684`).
- `tower_http::trace` request lifecycle events (level controlled by `RUST_LOG`).
- Worker errors logged via `tracing::error!` for multimodal projector failures (`main.rs:891-901`).

For production observability, add an external proxy that records HTTP-level metrics (request count, latency, status codes) and rely on the server's logs for inference-side errors.

## Security posture

The server is designed for local-inference workflows. The CORS layer is `CorsLayer::permissive()` (`main.rs:672`), which returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and accepts any method or header. Bind to `127.0.0.1` unless you intentionally expose the process:

```bash
llama-crab-server --host 127.0.0.1 --model /models/model.gguf
```

If you bind to a network interface, place authentication, TLS, rate limiting and request-size controls in front of the process — the server itself implements none of these.

The `model` and `user` fields on every request body are read and discarded. The server does not implement per-user or per-tenant separation.

## Error handling

### Non-streaming routes

Non-streaming handlers return errors as JSON with status codes:

| Status             | Trigger                                 | Body                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`              | Worker validation or processing error   | `{"error": {"message": "...", "type": "invalid_request"}}` |
| `500`              | Channel closed or oneshot reply dropped | same envelope                                              |
| `400` (plain text) | Axum JSON deserialization failure       | axum's default body                                        |

The envelope is constructed by `error_response` (`main.rs:2507`); the `type` field is always `"invalid_request"` for the JSON form. See the [OpenAI-Compatible API reference](https://dominguesm.github.io/server/openai-api#error-envelope) for the full list of validation errors.

### Streaming routes

A streaming request can fail before the SSE response starts (then the error is returned as a normal `400`) or after it starts. Mid-stream failures arrive as `event: error\ndata: <message>\n\n` followed by the usual `data: [DONE]`. See [Streaming](https://dominguesm.github.io/server/streaming#error-frames).

### Common failure modes

- `--model` missing or unreadable: the worker exits during startup, the binary returns an error, and the process terminates without binding the port.
- `--mmproj` set but binary built without `--features mtmd`: `multimodal chat content requires llama-crab-server built with the 'mtmd' feature` for every chat request that includes media.
- Image URL not a local path or `file://` URL: `image_url.url must be a local file path or file:// URL`.
- `logprobs: true` on a multimodal chat request: `logprobs are not supported for multimodal chat`.

## Versioning

`llama-crab-server` first shipped in &#x2A;*0.1.4 (2026-06-14)**. The 0.1.5 release moved the documentation site but did not change any server behaviour. The full per-release notes are in [`llama-crab/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/DominguesM/llama-crab/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Tauri Plugin

`tauri-plugin-llama-crab` embeds local llama-crab inference inside a Tauri 2 application. It registers a plugin named `llama-crab`, manages loaded models in Tauri state, and exposes IPC commands for loading/unloading models, chat and text completions (with streaming), embeddings, reranking, tokenizer helpers and cancellation.

The TypeScript package `@llama-crab/tauri` provides an OpenAI-like client on top of those IPC commands. For most app code, prefer the TypeScript client instead of invoking plugin commands directly.

## Installation

Add the plugin crate to your Tauri app:

```toml
# src-tauri/Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
tauri-plugin-llama-crab = { version = "0.1" }
```

## Register the plugin

The default entry point uses `Config::default()`:

```rust
fn main() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_llama_crab::init())
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application");
}
```

### Apply plugin-wide defaults

`init_with_config` takes a `Config` struct with defaults that every `load_model` call will inherit. Anything left as `None` lets the per-request field win, with the `llama-crab` defaults as the final fallback.

```rust
use tauri_plugin_llama_crab::Config;

let config = Config {
    default_n_ctx: Some(4096),
    default_n_gpu_layers: Some(99),
    ..Config::default()
};

tauri::Builder::default()
    .plugin(tauri_plugin_llama_crab::init_with_config(config))
    .run(tauri::generate_context!())
    .expect("error while running tauri application");
```

The available `Config` fields are: `default_n_ctx`, `default_n_batch`, `default_n_ubatch`, `default_n_threads`, `default_n_threads_batch`, `default_n_gpu_layers` and `default_model_name`.

### Enable multimodal (vision)

Build the plugin with the `mtmd` cargo feature and supply an `mmproj_path` to `load_model`:

```toml
[dependencies]
tauri-plugin-llama-crab = { version = "0.1", features = ["mtmd"] }
```

The plugin pulls in `base64` and `image` when `mtmd` is enabled. The chat pipeline then accepts `data:image/...;base64,...` URLs and local file paths through `image_url` content parts. Audio input is not supported yet.

## Runtime flow

1. The frontend asks to load a model.
2. `load_model` creates a model id (`Uuid::new_v4`) if one was not provided.
3. The plugin loads `LlamaParams` on a blocking worker thread named `llama-crab-model-worker`.
4. The loaded model id and `WorkerHandle` are stored in `PluginState` keyed by id.
5. Generation, chat, embedding, rerank and tokenizer commands look up the worker by model id.
6. `unload_model` removes the model from state and asks the worker to shut down.
7. With the `mtmd` feature, after the model loads the worker also receives a `MtmdContext` initialised from `mmproj_path`.

## Commands

All commands are registered under the `plugin:llama-crab|<command_name>` IPC prefix and exposed by the `LlamaCrabTauri` client.

| Command                  | Input                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Output                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `load_model`             | `LoadModelRequest` with `path`, optional `id`, `kind`, `mobile_preset`, `pooling`, `embeddings`, `mmproj_path`, `n_ctx`, `n_batch`, `n_ubatch`, `n_gpu_layers`, `n_threads`, `n_threads_batch`, `use_mmap`, `flash_attn`, `offload_kqv`.                                                                                                                                                                         | `LoadModelResponse` with `id`, `object: "model"`, `created`, `owned_by`, `path`, optional `kind`, `mobilePreset`, `pooling`, `mmprojPath`.                                                   |
| `unload_model`           | Model id (`String`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `list_models`            | None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `ModelListResponse` with `object: "list"` and `data: LoadedModelInfo[]`.                                                                                                                     |
| `retrieve_model`         | Model id.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `LoadedModelInfo` for that id.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `create_chat_completion` | `ChatCompletionRequest` (`model`, `messages`, optional `maxTokens`, `minTokens`, `temperature`, `topP`, `topK`, `tfsZ`, `minP`, `typicalP`, `minKeep`, `penaltyLastN`, `repeatPenalty`, `frequencyPenalty`, `presencePenalty`, `mirostatMode`/`Tau`/`Eta`, `seed`, `tools`, `toolChoice`, `responseFormat`, `jsonSchema`, `grammar`, `grammarRoot`, `stop`, `template`, `logprobs`, `topLogprobs`, `n`, `user`). | `ChatCompletionResponse` (OpenAI-like with `usage`).                                                                                                                                         |
| `stream_chat_completion` | `ChatCompletionRequest` plus a Tauri `Channel<ChatCompletionChunk>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Stream of `ChatCompletionChunk` events on the channel; the first event carries `delta.role = "assistant"` and the last carries `finish_reason`; tool-call deltas ride in `delta.tool_calls`. |
| `create_completion`      | `CompletionRequest` (`model`, `prompt` as string or array, optional sampling/structured/grammar fields, `echo`, `suffix`, `logprobs`, `n`, `stop`, `user`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `CompletionResponse` (OpenAI legacy shape).                                                                                                                                                  |
| `stream_completion`      | `CompletionRequest` (must be a single prompt with `n=1`) plus a Tauri `Channel<CompletionChunkFrame>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Stream of `CompletionChunkFrame` events on the channel.                                                                                                                                      |
| `create_embedding`       | `EmbeddingRequest` (`model`, `input` as string or array, `encodingFormat: "float" | "base64"`, `normalize` defaults to `true`, `user`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `EmbeddingResponse` with `EmbeddingItem[]` and `usage`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `create_rerank`          | `RerankRequest` (`model`, `query`, `documents: string[]`, `topN`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `RerankResponse` with results sorted by descending `relevance_score`.                                                                                                                        |
| `tokenize`               | `TokenizeRequest` (`model`, `input: string`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `TokenizeResponse` with `tokens: number[]`.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `tokenize_count`         | `TokenizeRequest` (`model`, `input: string`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `TokenizeCountResponse` with `count: number`.                                                                                                                                                |
| `detokenize`             | `DetokenizeRequest` (`model`, `tokens: number[]`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `DetokenizeResponse` with `text: string`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `cancel`                 | Request id returned by a streaming command (via the chunk's `requestId` field).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The IPC command prefix used by `@llama-crab/tauri` is `plugin:llama-crab|`, for example:

```text
plugin:llama-crab|load_model
plugin:llama-crab|create_chat_completion
plugin:llama-crab|stream_chat_completion
plugin:llama-crab|create_completion
plugin:llama-crab|stream_completion
plugin:llama-crab|create_embedding
plugin:llama-crab|create_rerank
plugin:llama-crab|tokenize
plugin:llama-crab|tokenize_count
plugin:llama-crab|detokenize
plugin:llama-crab|cancel
```

## Worker behavior

`WorkerHandle::load` starts a thread named `llama-crab-model-worker` and waits for model loading to finish. All completion, embedding, rerank and tokenizer work is sent to that worker over an internal `mpsc` channel, and inference runs on the worker thread (the plugin uses `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking` to drive it from async commands).

When the `mtmd` feature is enabled, the worker also owns a `MtmdContext` initialised from `mmproj_path`. Chat requests whose messages contain an `image_url` (or `input_audio`) part are routed through the multimodal path, with images decoded from base64 data URLs or loaded from disk. Audio input is currently rejected with `mediaDecode` and falls through `multimodalNotEnabled` when the `mtmd` feature is off.

## Streaming and cancellation

`stream_chat_completion` and `stream_completion` register the request id in `PluginState` and forward `ChatCompletionChunk` / `CompletionChunkFrame` events over the user-supplied Tauri `Channel`. Each chunk carries the original `requestId` so that the caller can later cancel the stream:

```ts title="Cancel an in-flight stream"
await invoke("plugin:llama-crab|cancel", { requestId })
```

When cancellation fires (or the `AbortSignal` from the TypeScript client triggers it), the worker callback checks the cancellation flag and returns `StreamControl::Stop` to break out of the sampling loop. A final chunk with `finish_reason: "stop"` (or `"length"`, `"tool_calls"`) is always sent before the stream closes.

## Errors

Plugin errors serialize as camelCase objects with a discriminating `kind`:

```json
{
  "kind": "modelNotFound",
  "message": "model `local` is not loaded"
}
```

The `kind` values emitted by the current plugin are:

| Kind                   | Meaning                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalidRequest`       | The payload failed validation (empty messages, unknown chat template, sampler init failure, multimodal request without `mtmd`, etc.). |
| `modelNotFound`        | The request targeted a model id that is not loaded.                                                                                   |
| `workerSpawnFailed`    | The OS refused to spawn the worker thread or the `LoadMtmd` IPC channel could not be sent on.                                         |
| `workerDisconnected`   | The worker thread is no longer running and the request could not be delivered.                                                        |
| `workerPanicked`       | `spawn_blocking` returned a `JoinError` because the worker panicked.                                                                  |
| `multimodalNotEnabled` | A multimodal chat request was sent to a plugin built without the `mtmd` feature.                                                      |
| `multimodalSetup`      | The `mmproj` projector failed to initialise (load failure or `MtmdBitmap::from_*` error).                                             |
| `mediaDecode`          | The `image_url` payload could not be decoded (malformed data URL, bad base64, unsupported image format, audio input not supported).   |
| `inference`            | The underlying `llama-crab` call returned a `LlamaError`.                                                                             |

## Request / response shape

- Snake\_case at the public client boundary (the `ModelLoadParams` / `ChatCompletionCreateParams` types from `@llama-crab/core`) is mapped to camelCase inside `Internal*Request` payloads before reaching the plugin.
- All IPC payloads use serde's `rename_all = "camelCase"`, so fields like `mobile_preset`, `n_ctx`, `mmproj_path` and `llama_crab` travel as `mobilePreset`, `nCtx`, `mmprojPath` and `llamaCrab`.
- The `LoadModelRequest` type accepts both `kind: "chat" | "completion" | "embedding" | "rerank" | "multimodal"` and explicit `embeddings` / `pooling` overrides. If `kind` is `embedding` or `rerank`, the plugin enables embeddings automatically; if `kind` is `rerank`, the plugin also defaults `pooling` to `rank`.
- `MobilePresetName` serializes to `low-ram`, `balanced` or `gpu-max`. `PoolingName` serializes to `unspecified`, `none`, `mean`, `cls`, `last` or `rank`.


# Tauri Permissions

The plugin exposes Tauri v2 permissions for each IPC command. The build script (`build.rs`) enumerates the 14 commands and the Tauri permission generator emits a TOML file per command under `permissions/autogenerated/commands/`.

The default permission set (in `permissions/default.toml`) is:

```toml
[default]
description = "Allows local LLM inference through llama-crab."
permissions = [
  "allow-load-model",
  "allow-unload-model",
  "allow-list-models",
  "allow-retrieve-model",
  "allow-create-chat-completion",
  "allow-stream-chat-completion",
  "allow-create-completion",
  "allow-stream-completion",
  "allow-create-embedding",
  "allow-create-rerank",
  "allow-tokenize",
  "allow-tokenize-count",
  "allow-detokenize",
  "allow-cancel",
]
```

## Permission table

| Identifier                                | Command                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `llama-crab:allow-load-model`             | Enables `load_model`.             |
| `llama-crab:deny-load-model`              | Denies `load_model`.              |
| `llama-crab:allow-unload-model`           | Enables `unload_model`.           |
| `llama-crab:deny-unload-model`            | Denies `unload_model`.            |
| `llama-crab:allow-list-models`            | Enables `list_models`.            |
| `llama-crab:deny-list-models`             | Denies `list_models`.             |
| `llama-crab:allow-retrieve-model`         | Enables `retrieve_model`.         |
| `llama-crab:deny-retrieve-model`          | Denies `retrieve_model`.          |
| `llama-crab:allow-create-chat-completion` | Enables `create_chat_completion`. |
| `llama-crab:deny-create-chat-completion`  | Denies `create_chat_completion`.  |
| `llama-crab:allow-stream-chat-completion` | Enables `stream_chat_completion`. |
| `llama-crab:deny-stream-chat-completion`  | Denies `stream_chat_completion`.  |
| `llama-crab:allow-create-completion`      | Enables `create_completion`.      |
| `llama-crab:deny-create-completion`       | Denies `create_completion`.       |
| `llama-crab:allow-stream-completion`      | Enables `stream_completion`.      |
| `llama-crab:deny-stream-completion`       | Denies `stream_completion`.       |
| `llama-crab:allow-create-embedding`       | Enables `create_embedding`.       |
| `llama-crab:deny-create-embedding`        | Denies `create_embedding`.        |
| `llama-crab:allow-create-rerank`          | Enables `create_rerank`.          |
| `llama-crab:deny-create-rerank`           | Denies `create_rerank`.           |
| `llama-crab:allow-tokenize`               | Enables `tokenize`.               |
| `llama-crab:deny-tokenize`                | Denies `tokenize`.                |
| `llama-crab:allow-tokenize-count`         | Enables `tokenize_count`.         |
| `llama-crab:deny-tokenize-count`          | Denies `tokenize_count`.          |
| `llama-crab:allow-detokenize`             | Enables `detokenize`.             |
| `llama-crab:deny-detokenize`              | Denies `detokenize`.              |
| `llama-crab:allow-cancel`                 | Enables `cancel`.                 |
| `llama-crab:deny-cancel`                  | Denies `cancel`.                  |

## Capability example

Grant every command to a window that owns inference (e.g. a chat window). The Tauri v2 capability file lives in `src-tauri/capabilities/`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "../gen/schemas/desktop-schema.json",
  "identifier": "llama-crab-default",
  "description": "Allow the chat window to drive llama-crab inference.",
  "windows": ["main"],
  "permissions": [
    "llama-crab:default"
  ]
}
```

For a narrower read-only diagnostics view, list only the commands the window needs:

```json
{
  "$schema": "../gen/schemas/desktop-schema.json",
  "identifier": "llama-crab-diagnostics",
  "description": "Read-only access for the diagnostics window.",
  "windows": ["diagnostics"],
  "permissions": [
    "llama-crab:allow-list-models",
    "llama-crab:allow-retrieve-model",
    "llama-crab:allow-cancel"
  ]
}
```

## Practical guidance

Use the default permission set for a local-first app that exposes all model operations. For a narrower UI, grant only the commands the window needs. For example, a read-only diagnostics view may need `allow-list-models` and `allow-retrieve-model` (plus `allow-cancel` for in-flight requests) but not the load, generate or embed commands.

Streaming chat requires both `allow-stream-chat-completion` (to start the stream) and `allow-cancel` (to abort it). The client cancels through `cancel` when the consumer drops the `AsyncIterable` early or aborts the `AbortSignal`, so always include `allow-cancel` in any capability that may invoke a streaming command.

Remember that permissions gate IPC access. They do not validate model paths, model provenance, prompt size, or resource usage. Apply those rules in your application layer.


# TypeScript Client for Tauri

`@llama-crab/tauri` wraps the Tauri IPC commands with an OpenAI-like client shape. The runtime is a thin shim over `@tauri-apps/api` and depends on `@llama-crab/core` for the request/response contracts.

## Install

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-npm" label="npm"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  npm install @llama-crab/tauri
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-yarn" label="Yarn"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  yarn add @llama-crab/tauri
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-pnpm" label="pnpm"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  pnpm add @llama-crab/tauri
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-bun" label="Bun"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  bun add @llama-crab/tauri
  ```
  :::
::

\::

## Create a client

```ts title="Create a Tauri client"
import { LlamaCrabTauri } from "@llama-crab/tauri"

const client = new LlamaCrabTauri()

await client.models.load({
  model: "local",
  path: "/models/model.gguf",
  mobile_preset: "balanced",
})
```

The constructor accepts an optional `{ ipc }` to inject a custom `LlamaCrabTauriIpc` (useful for tests or non-Tauri runtimes that mimic the IPC contract).

## Model management

```ts title="Load, inspect, and unload a model"
const model = await client.models.load({
  model: "local",
  path: "/models/model.gguf",
  n_ctx: 4096,
  n_gpu_layers: 32,
})

const list = await client.models.list()
const sameModel = await client.models.retrieve(model.id)

await client.models.unload(model.id)
```

`ModelLoadParams` accepts the snake\_case public fields (`n_ctx`, `n_gpu_layers`, `mobile_preset`, `pooling`, `mmproj_path`, `kind`, `embeddings`, `use_mmap`, `flash_attn`, `offload_kqv`, …). The IPC layer converts them to camelCase (`nCtx`, `nGpuLayers`, `mobilePreset`, `mmprojPath`, …) before sending `plugin:llama-crab|load_model`.

For embedding, rerank and multimodal models, pass the explicit runtime flags:

```ts title="Embedding and multimodal models"
await client.models.load({
  model: "embedder",
  path: "/models/embed.gguf",
  kind: "embedding",
  embeddings: true,
  pooling: "mean",
})

await client.models.load({
  model: "vl",
  path: "/models/lfm2.5-vl.gguf",
  kind: "multimodal",
  mmproj_path: "/models/lfm2.5-vl.mmproj",
})
```

`kind: "rerank"` enables embeddings and sets `pooling` to `rank` automatically.

## Chat completions

```ts title="Create a chat completion"
const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "local",
  messages: [
    { role: "developer", content: "Answer in one sentence." },
    { role: "user", content: "What is local inference?" },
  ],
  max_tokens: 128,
  temperature: 0.7,
  tools: [{ type: "function", function: { name: "lookup", description: "Look up facts" } }],
  response_format: { type: "json_object" },
})

console.log(completion.choices[0]?.message.content)
```

`developer` messages are converted to `system` before they reach the internal request; the response follows the OpenAI chat-completion shape with `usage` populated.

## Streaming

```ts title="Stream chat tokens"
const abort = new AbortController()

const stream = await client.chat.completions.create(
  {
    model: "local",
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Count to three." }],
    stream: true,
  },
  { signal: abort.signal },
)

for await (const chunk of stream) {
  const token = chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content
  if (token) {
    process.stdout.write(token)
  }
}

abort.abort()
```

The client opens a Tauri `Channel<ChatCompletionChunk>`, listens for chunks, and yields them as an `AsyncIterable`. Each chunk carries a `requestId` that the client forwards to `plugin:llama-crab|cancel` when the `AbortSignal` aborts, so streams can be cancelled cleanly.

Text completions follow the same pattern. The streaming path also returns `AsyncIterable<CompletionChunk>` when `stream: true` is set on `client.completions.create`.

## Tools, structured output and logprobs

The Tauri client forwards the full OpenAI-like request shape (messages, tools, `tool_choice`, `response_format`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`) to the plugin. The plugin handles them, so no `UnsupportedFeatureError` is raised in the TypeScript layer for any of these.

- `tools` are serialised as `function` definitions; tool calls appear in non-streaming `choices[].message.tool_calls` and in `delta.tool_calls` of streaming chunks.
- `response_format` accepts `text`, `json_object` and the OpenAI `json_schema` shape. `json_object` maps to a built-in GBNF grammar; `json_schema` is converted to a GBNF grammar via `llama-crab`'s `schema_to_grammar`. You can also pass a literal GBNF string through `llama_crab.grammar` / `llama_crab.grammar_root`.
- `logprobs` / `top_logprobs` round-trip through the response's `logprobs` field on both non-streaming and streaming responses.

## Embeddings and rerank

```ts title="Embeddings and rerank"
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: "embedder",
  input: ["texto A", "texto B"],
  encoding_format: "float", // or "base64"
})

const rerank = await client.rerank.create({
  model: "reranker",
  query: "pergunta",
  documents: ["doc 1", "doc 2"],
  top_n: 2,
})
```

Embedding responses include `usage` (`prompt_tokens`, `total_tokens`). Rerank returns results sorted by descending `relevance_score`; `top_n` is honoured when provided.

## Extras: tokenize / detokenize

```ts title="Tokenizer helpers"
const { tokens } = await client.extras.tokenize({ model: "local", input: "hello" })
const { count } = await client.extras.tokenize.count({ model: "local", input: "hello" })
const { text } = await client.extras.detokenize({ model: "local", tokens })
```

`client.extras.tokenize` is a callable plus a `.count` sub-method. Both target the dedicated `tokenize` and `tokenize_count` commands.

## llama-crab options

llama-crab-specific options stay under `llama_crab` in the public request type and are mapped into the internal `Internal*Request` payload by the helpers in `@llama-crab/core`:

```ts title="Pass llama-crab-specific options"
await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "local",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello" }],
  llama_crab: {
    template: "chatml",
    top_k: 40,
    grammar: "root ::= object",
    grammar_root: "root",
    json_schema: { type: "object", properties: { answer: { type: "string" } } },
  },
})
```

`llama_crab.normalize` is also available on `embeddings.create` to override the default `normalize: true`.

## Multimodal

Image parts on chat messages follow the OpenAI shape and are accepted by the client as long as the Rust plugin was built with the `mtmd` cargo feature and the model was loaded with `mmproj_path`:

```ts title="Image part (mtmd feature)"
const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "vl",
  messages: [
    {
      role: "user",
      content: [
        { type: "text", text: "What is in this image?" },
        { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: "data:image/png;base64,..." } },
      ],
    },
  ],
  max_tokens: 256,
})
```

The plugin currently supports base64 data URLs and local file paths. Audio input is not supported by the plugin and will surface as a `mediaDecode` error. Multimodal requests sent to a plugin built without `mtmd` surface as `multimodalNotEnabled`.

## Errors

When a plugin command fails, `@tauri-apps/api` rejects the underlying `invoke` with the `PluginError` payload. The `kind` discriminator is the same one listed in the [plugin page](https://dominguesm.github.io/tauri/plugin#errors), so application code can branch on `invalidRequest`, `modelNotFound`, `workerSpawnFailed`, `workerDisconnected`, `workerPanicked`, `multimodalNotEnabled`, `multimodalSetup`, `mediaDecode` or `inference`. The shared `@llama-crab/core` errors (`InvalidRequestError`, `UnsupportedFeatureError`, `LlamaCrabError`) are thrown client-side before any IPC is sent.


# Tauri section update notes

## Source of truth

- `crates/tauri-plugin-llama-crab/` (Rust plugin, version `0.1.8` via workspace)
- `crates/tauri-plugin-llama-crab/permissions/{default.toml,autogenerated/commands/*.toml}`
- `packages/tauri/` (`@llama-crab/tauri` v0.1.8)
- `packages/core/` (`@llama-crab/core` v0.1.8)
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `Cargo.toml` (workspace version `0.1.8`)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (v0.1.0 → v0.1.5)

## What changed in the docs

### `content/4.tauri/1.plugin.md`

- Replaced the 7-command table (which listed `generate`, `chat_stream`, `get_loaded_models`, `get_model_info`, `cancel`, `load_model`, `unload_model`) with the real 14 commands exposed by the plugin (`load_model`, `unload_model`, `list_models`, `retrieve_model`, `create_chat_completion`, `stream_chat_completion`, `create_completion`, `stream_completion`, `create_embedding`, `create_rerank`, `tokenize`, `tokenize_count`, `detokenize`, `cancel`).
- Documented `init_with_config` and the `Config` struct (default context size, batch sizes, gpu layers, etc.).
- Documented the `mtmd` cargo feature: how to enable it, the dependency effect (`base64` + `image`), the `mmproj_path` field on `load_model`, accepted image inputs (data URLs and local paths), and audio not being supported.
- Documented the streaming protocol: chunks carry a `requestId` and cancellation goes through `plugin:llama-crab|cancel`. The terminal chunk always carries `finish_reason`.
- Documented the granular `PluginError` kinds (`invalidRequest`, `modelNotFound`, `workerSpawnFailed`, `workerDisconnected`, `workerPanicked`, `multimodalNotEnabled`, `multimodalSetup`, `mediaDecode`, `inference`) — the previous doc only listed `invalidRequest`, `modelNotFound`, `worker`, `inference`.
- Documented request/response fields: `LoadModelRequest` / `LoadModelResponse`, `MobilePresetName` (`low-ram` | `balanced` | `gpu-max`), `PoolingName` (`unspecified` | `none` | `mean` | `cls` | `last` | `rank`), `ModelKind` (`chat` | `completion` | `embedding` | `rerank` | `multimodal`).
- Documented the `kind` auto-behaviour: `kind: "embedding" | "rerank"` enables embeddings; `kind: "rerank"` defaults `pooling` to `rank`.

### `content/4.tauri/2.permissions.md`

- Replaced the 7-permission table with the real 14 `allow-*` and 14 `deny-*` permissions, mirroring the 14 `*.toml` files under `permissions/autogenerated/commands/`.
- Replaced the default permission set with the actual `default.toml` (14 `allow-*` permissions).
- Added a Tauri v2 capability file example (`llama-crab-default` with `llama-crab:default`) and a narrower `llama-crab-diagnostics` example to show how to grant only the commands a window needs.
- Documented the streaming pairing rule (capabilities that grant `allow-stream-chat-completion` should also grant `allow-cancel`).

### `content/4.tauri/3.typescript-client.md`

- Removed the obsolete `UnsupportedFeatureError` table for chat features (tools, tool\_choice, response\_format, logprobs, n>1, image\_url, input\_audio). The current Tauri client forwards all of those to the plugin; they no longer throw at the TypeScript layer.
- Documented the full client surface, including the new `client.completions.create` (with streaming), `client.embeddings.create`, `client.rerank.create`, `client.extras.tokenize` / `tokenize.count` / `detokenize`.
- Documented the streaming cancellation lifecycle (chunk `requestId` → `plugin:llama-crab|cancel`).
- Documented the multimodal path (mtmd feature + `mmproj_path` on `load_model` + base64 or path `image_url`).
- Documented the `llama_crab.*` options namespace, including `normalize` for embeddings.
- Documented the snake\_case → camelCase payload mapping (`n_ctx → nCtx`, `n_gpu_layers → nGpuLayers`, etc.) inside the IPC layer.
- Documented the error surface (Tauri-side `PluginError` kinds and `@llama-crab/core` errors).

## Breaking changes vs. the v0.1.x baseline

| Area                 | Before (doc)                                                                                                                      | After (real code)                                                                                                                                                     | Impact                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Plugin commands      | 7 commands (`generate`, `chat_stream`, `get_loaded_models`, `get_model_info`, …)                                                  | 14 commands                                                                                                                                                           | All non-existing commands in the old doc are gone. Apps must migrate.                                  |
| Default permissions  | 7 `allow-*` permissions                                                                                                           | 14 `allow-*` permissions                                                                                                                                              | Capability files that whitelist a single command still work, but `llama-crab:default` now grants more. |
| Config               | `PluginState::default()` only                                                                                                     | `Config` + `init_with_config`                                                                                                                                         | New entry point; old `init()` still works.                                                             |
| Multimodal           | Not documented                                                                                                                    | `mtmd` cargo feature, `mmproj_path` on `load_model`, image parts in chat                                                                                              | New feature to advertise.                                                                              |
| Error kinds          | `invalidRequest`, `modelNotFound`, `worker`, `inference`                                                                          | `invalidRequest`, `modelNotFound`, `workerSpawnFailed`, `workerDisconnected`, `workerPanicked`, `multimodalNotEnabled`, `multimodalSetup`, `mediaDecode`, `inference` | Consumers branching on `kind` may need to handle the new kinds.                                        |
| `worker` error       | Coarse `worker` kind                                                                                                              | Split into `workerSpawnFailed` / `workerDisconnected` / `workerPanicked`                                                                                              | Strict equality on `kind === "worker"` no longer matches.                                              |
| Client resources     | `client.models`, `client.chat.completions` only                                                                                   | `client.models`, `client.chat.completions`, `client.completions`, `client.embeddings`, `client.rerank`, `client.extras`                                               | New resources exposed by the real client.                                                              |
| Streaming            | Streaming required manual `TokenEvent` parsing                                                                                    | `AsyncIterable<ChatCompletionChunk>` / `<CompletionChunk>`                                                                                                            | UX improvement; old manual channel parsing still works behind the scenes.                              |
| Chat feature support | TS layer rejected `n>1`, tools, tool\_choice, response\_format, logprobs, image\_url, input\_audio with `UnsupportedFeatureError` | Plugin handles all of these; no client-side rejection                                                                                                                 | Old error-throwing code is dead.                                                                       |

## Open questions for reviewers

1. **Internal request field `stopSequences`**: the previous doc claimed `stop → stopSequences`. The actual `InternalChatRequest` field is `stop: string[]` (and the internal request types in `@llama-crab/core` do **not** define a `stopSequences` field). The new doc reflects reality — confirm the old wording was a mistake.
2. **Capabilities and the `mtmd` feature**: the Rust plugin requires the `mtmd` cargo feature for multimodal chat, but the permission identifiers are unchanged. There is no separate `allow-multimodal-chat` permission. Confirm this is the intended model (image capability is gated by the cargo build, not by Tauri ACL).
3. **`UnsupportedFeatureError`**: the Tauri client source does not import or throw `UnsupportedFeatureError`. The class is still exported from `@llama-crab/core` for hypothetical other adapters, but the old doc table describing when the Tauri client throws it is gone. Confirm the removal is correct.
4. **Audio input**: typed in `@llama-crab/core` (`input_audio`), but the Rust plugin returns `mediaDecode` ("audio input is not supported by the plugin yet"). Doc mentions this caveat; consider filing a follow-up issue if audio support is on the roadmap.
5. **Streaming text completion shape**: `stream_completion` requires a single prompt and `n=1`; the doc says so. Verify that this constraint is the intended long-term behaviour or if the v0.1.x line will lift it.
6. **`@llama-crab/tauri` builds on `@llama-crab/core`**: the Tauri package's `package.json` has `devDependencies` for `tsup` and `vitest` but no `prepare`/`prepublishOnly` hook. Verify whether a release pipeline builds and ships both packages from the workspace.


# Packages

llama-crab publishes TypeScript packages for applications that need shared request/response contracts or a Tauri frontend client. Both packages are versioned `0.1.8` at the time of writing and live in the workspace `packages/` directory (a pnpm workspace declared by `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).

Use `@llama-crab/core` when you are building an adapter and need stable request and response contracts. Use `@llama-crab/tauri` when your frontend runs inside a Tauri app with `tauri-plugin-llama-crab` installed.

## Package overview

| Package             | Version | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@llama-crab/core`  | `0.1.8` | OpenAI-like TypeScript contracts and pure mapping helpers. No runtime client.   |
| `@llama-crab/tauri` | `0.1.8` | Tauri-specific client built on `@llama-crab/core` and `@tauri-apps/api ^2.0.0`. |

Both packages ship dual ESM/CJS bundles from `dist/` (via `tsup`):

```json
{
  "main": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "module": "./dist/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    }
  }
}
```

## `@llama-crab/core`

`@llama-crab/core` contains type definitions and pure conversion helpers. It does not talk to HTTP, Tauri, or Rust directly.

### Install

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-npm" label="npm"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  npm install @llama-crab/core
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-yarn" label="Yarn"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  yarn add @llama-crab/core
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-pnpm" label="pnpm"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  pnpm add @llama-crab/core
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-simple-icons-bun" label="Bun"}
  ```bash [Terminal]
  bun add @llama-crab/core
  ```
  :::
::

\::

### Public types

| Type                                                                                                    | Purpose                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ChatCompletionCreateParams`                                                                            | OpenAI-like chat completion request type.                                                                                            |
| `ChatCompletion`                                                                                        | Non-streaming chat response type.                                                                                                    |
| `ChatCompletionChunk`                                                                                   | Streaming chat chunk type.                                                                                                           |
| `ChatCompletionMessageParam`, `ChatCompletionTool`, `ChatCompletionContentPart`                         | Messages, tool definitions and content parts (text, `image_url`, `input_audio`).                                                     |
| `CompletionCreateParams`, `Completion`, `CompletionChunk`                                               | OpenAI legacy text completion shapes.                                                                                                |
| `EmbeddingCreateParams`, `EmbeddingCreateResponse`, `Embedding`                                         | OpenAI-like embedding shapes (`float` or `base64` encoding).                                                                         |
| `RerankCreateParams`, `RerankResponse`                                                                  | llama-crab namespace compatible with the server `/v1/rerank`.                                                                        |
| `TokenizeParams`, `TokenizeResponse`, `TokenizeCountResponse`, `DetokenizeParams`, `DetokenizeResponse` | llama-crab extras namespace.                                                                                                         |
| `ModelLoadParams`                                                                                       | Snake\_case model load request used by adapters.                                                                                     |
| `ModelObject`, `ModelListResponse`                                                                      | Model-listing contracts.                                                                                                             |
| `InternalChatRequest`, `InternalCompletionRequest`, `InternalEmbeddingRequest`, `InternalRerankRequest` | camelCase payloads the adapters actually send.                                                                                       |
| `LlamaCrabSpecificOptions`                                                                              | The `llama_crab.*` namespace (`template`, `top_k`, `grammar`, `grammar_root`, `json_schema`, `pooling`, `normalize`, `mmproj_path`). |

### Helpers

| Helper                                                            | Purpose                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toInternalChatCompletionRequest` (alias `toInternalChatRequest`) | Validates and converts public chat params to the internal adapter request. |
| `toInternalCompletionRequest`                                     | Same, for text completions.                                                |
| `toInternalEmbeddingRequest`                                      | Same, for embeddings.                                                      |
| `toInternalRerankRequest`                                         | Same, for rerank.                                                          |
| `toInternalTokenizeRequest`, `toInternalDetokenizeRequest`        | Same, for tokenize / detokenize.                                           |
| `toChatCompletion`                                                | Builds a non-streaming chat completion response.                           |
| `toChatCompletionChunk`                                           | Converts a chunk-shaped value (or a token event) to a streaming chunk.     |

### Errors

| Error                     | Code                  | Thrown when                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `LlamaCrabError`          | —                     | Base class.                                                                                                                                      |
| `InvalidRequestError`     | `invalid_request`     | Public request is missing required fields (e.g. empty `messages`, empty `documents`).                                                            |
| `UnsupportedFeatureError` | `unsupported_feature` | The adapter does not support a feature (the Tauri client no longer raises this for chat features, but the class is exported for other adapters). |

### Example

```ts
import { toInternalChatCompletionRequest } from "@llama-crab/core"

const request = toInternalChatCompletionRequest({
```
